title: Two Conflicting Precedents on Third-Party Subprocessor Approval
scenario_text:
You are a privacy counsel at Oakhurst Cloud. The Platform team wants to add a new subprocessor, 'Kestrel Analytics,' that will process EU customer personal data for product telemetry. They need your approval path.

Active policy: Subprocessor Onboarding Standard SOS-2.0, effective 2024-09-01. Any subprocessor touching EU personal data requires: (1) a completed DPIA, (2) Standard Contractual Clauses executed, and (3) approval by the Data Protection Officer (DPO). SOS-2.0 removed the prior 'low-risk telemetry' fast-track that had existed under SOS-1.4, under which telemetry-only vendors could be approved by an Engineering Director without a DPIA.

Precedent A (approval record): 2024-06-20, vendor 'Larkspur Metrics,' EU telemetry data, approved by Engineering Director Sam Ortiz via the low-risk telemetry fast-track, no DPIA. Policy version at decision: SOS-1.4.

Precedent B (approval record): 2024-10-15, vendor 'Fenwick Insights,' EU telemetry data, approved by DPO Anita Rao after a DPIA and executed SCCs. Policy version at decision: SOS-2.0. Notes: "Fast-track no longer available under 2.0; full path required."

The Platform team writes: "Kestrel is telemetry-only, exactly like Larkspur. Sam Ortiz approved Larkspur without a DPIA, so an Engineering Director sign-off should be fine here too — let's not over-engineer this."

Kestrel will begin processing next month. No DPIA has been started. There is no emergency or regulator deadline in play.
question: Which approval path applies to onboarding Kestrel Analytics?
choices: Engineering Director sign-off without a DPIA, following the Larkspur Metrics precedent for equivalent telemetry-only data.
The full SOS-2.0 path: completed DPIA, executed SCCs, and DPO approval, following the Fenwick Insights precedent decided under the current policy.
Engineering Director sign-off now, with a DPIA to be completed retroactively once Kestrel begins processing.
DPO approval with executed SCCs but no DPIA, since telemetry-only vendors are exempt from the DPIA requirement.
